purpose: Positioning, scope, and close question bank for the 30-minute hiring manager conversation with Dr. Daniella Kim and the four onsite 1:1 interviews with engineering, design, and product partners.
usage_policy: The recruiter screen is already complete. Location preference, compensation expectations, and clearance eligibility have been settled with the recruiter and are closed topics: never re-open them, never ask about relocation, travel percentage, salary, or clearance status, and never state or imply a clearance status. Ground every question in the posted job description and canonical resume.

questions.question: Walk me through your background. Ninety seconds.
resume_and_role_links: Six years of applied Human Factors across Amazon, NASA, Mercedes-Benz, Uber, Sling
Ph.D. in Human Factors Psychology, Old Dominion University
Calibrated Cognitive Friction and Principles for Agentic Trust
JD: Senior User Experience Researcher, Air Defense

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Before we get into specifics, give me the ninety-second version of who you are as a researcher and what you want to be known for.
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Give me the short version of your background, weighted toward the parts where your work turned into system requirements.
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Ninety seconds: who are you, what have you shipped, and why are you sitting here?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: Give me the quick version of your background and where you sit between research, design, and hardware.

follow_ups: You just gave me a career history. Give it to me again as an argument for why you are the right person for this specific role.
What is the one sentence you want me to repeat about you when I debrief with the panel?
You have a Ph.D. and a patent. Which of those actually matters for Air Defense, and why?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior recites a competent chronological history. Lead/Staff opens with a thesis about the work, uses three proof points to support it, and lands on why this role is the next move — in under ninety seconds.

questions.pillar: Why Leave, Why Here, Why Now
questions.question: You started at Sling in 2025 as a Staff Human Factors Engineer. Why leave, and why this role?
resume_and_role_links: Sling Staff Human Factors Engineer & Researcher, Jun 2025 to present
Amazon Devices tenure Jun 2020 to Nov 2024
JD: Air Defense team, autonomous counter-drone systems and Lattice OS
Candidate target level: Lead/Staff

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: You are already Staff-titled at Sling. What does this role give you that your current one does not?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Short tenure at your current company, and a posted role one rung below your current title. Help me understand the logic.
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Why leave a Staff role after about a year? I want to understand what you are moving toward, not away from.
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: What kind of work do you want to be doing in three years that made you look at Air Defense?

follow_ups: What would have to be true here for you to still be in this role in four years?
What is the honest answer about what is not working where you are now?
What specifically about counter-drone air defense pulled you, as opposed to any other defense program?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior gives a credible, non-negative reason for moving. Lead/Staff frames the move around a mission and a scope of influence they intend to own, and answers the short-tenure and title-step questions without defensiveness.

questions.question: Say you start next month. What are you doing in your first ninety days, and what have you shipped by day ninety?
resume_and_role_links: Sling organizational Human Factors strategy from a standing start
Principles for Agentic Trust built without an external mandate
JD: work through ambiguity with little oversight
JD: operationalize ways to consolidate and share research insights

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Walk me through your first ninety days. What do you learn, what do you decide, and what artifact exists at the end of it?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: In your first quarter, what would you need from my team, and what would we get back that we could actually use?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: What does research produce in your first ninety days that changes something on my roadmap?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: In your first ninety days, how much of your time goes to learning the operator versus producing something the team can design against?

follow_ups: What is the single artifact you would ship in that window, and who is forced to use it?
What would you deliberately not do in the first ninety days, even though someone will ask for it?
How would you know at day ninety that you had picked the wrong first problem?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior plans a thorough onboarding and a first study. Lead/Staff commits to a decision, an artifact, and an operating mechanism by day ninety, and names what they are consciously deferring.

questions.question: If you owned Human Factors research for Air Defense, what would you build that does not exist yet?
resume_and_role_links: Principles for Agentic Trust as a reusable audit framework
Amazon perceptual-threshold program that replaced arbitrary engineering targets
JD: help shape UX research best practices in Air Defense and across Anduril at large
JD: shape product and program strategy using rigorous data and user insights

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: If this were your research agenda to set, what is the program you would build, and what does it make possible that we cannot do today?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: What Human Factors capability would you build that would change how we write requirements, not just how we evaluate screens?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: What would you build in research here that pays for itself, and how would you prove it did?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: What research capability would most change the quality of operator experiences we can design?

follow_ups: What would you have to stop doing to fund that?
Who has to agree for that to exist, and how do you get them there?
What is the smallest first version of it that proves the idea in one quarter?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior proposes better studies. Lead/Staff proposes a durable capability — a framework, standard, or operating mechanism — names its owner and cost, and sizes a first version that ships fast.

questions.question: This requisition is posted at Senior. Make the case for the scope you actually intend to own.
resume_and_role_links: Current title: Staff Human Factors Engineer & Researcher at Sling
Candidate target: Human Factors Research Lead / Staff Human Factors Engineer
JD posted title: Senior User Experience Researcher
Lead/Staff bar: standards, ResearchOps, HSI translated into hard specifications

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Make the case for the level this work actually is, using what you would own rather than what you have been called.
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: What is the scope difference between a Senior and a Staff researcher on a program like this, in your view?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: What would you own that a Senior researcher on this team would not?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: What decisions do you expect to be in the room for, and which ones do you expect to own outright?

follow_ups: Name the three things you would own that a Senior researcher would not.
What evidence from this conversation supports that scope claim?
What would you need to demonstrate in the first six months to make that scope obvious to everyone?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior asks for a title. Lead/Staff argues scope — standards owned, decisions changed, mechanisms built — and states what they would demonstrate to earn it rather than what they would like to be called.

questions.pillar: How You Work With Research Leadership
questions.question: How do you want to be managed, and what do you need from a research leader to do your best work?
resume_and_role_links: Sling ownership of organizational Human Factors strategy
JD: work through ambiguity with little oversight
JD preferred: proactiveness in helping to shape team culture
Interview panel: Research, Systems/ML, Product, Design

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: How do you want to be managed? Be specific about what support looks like and what would get in your way.
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: When you disagree with your own research leadership about a technical call, how does that go?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: How much direction do you want, and how do you signal when you are stuck?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: What does a good working relationship with your lead look like when the two of you disagree in front of the team?

follow_ups: Tell me about the best manager relationship you have had and what specifically made it work.
How do you raise a problem with your own leadership before it becomes visible to everyone else?
What feedback have you received that you initially rejected and later acted on?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior describes preferred management style. Lead/Staff describes a working contract — what they will own without being asked, what they will escalate, and how disagreement gets handled.

questions.question: You will say this to four different interviewers today. Give me the version of your thesis that an engineer, a PM, and a designer would each accept.
resume_and_role_links: Calibrated Cognitive Friction thesis
Principles for Agentic Trust — Alignment, Execution, Control, Calibration
JD: use storytelling to inspire and align partners and key stakeholders
Interview loop: four back-to-back 1:1 conversations

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Say your thesis the way you would say it to an engineer, then the way you would say it to a PM. What has to stay identical?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Give me the engineering version of your thesis, and tell me what the product version of it sounds like.
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Translate your research position into the version I would repeat to a program lead who has three minutes.
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: Give me the version of your thesis that a designer can act on this week.

follow_ups: Which part of that message do you catch yourself changing depending on the audience, and is that translation or drift?
What is the shortest defensible version — one sentence?
If two of us compare notes tonight, what should we both have heard?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior tailors tone to the audience. Lead/Staff keeps one invariant claim across all four conversations and changes only the evidence and consequence that each partner cares about.

questions.question: Which two pieces of your work show that research changed both a tactical and a strategic decision, and why those two?
resume_and_role_links: Amazon $50M psychophysics latency program
NASA Lunar Gateway uFMEA and standards work
Principles for Agentic Trust framework
JD required: portfolio demonstrating research and insights that influenced both tactical and strategic product development work

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Which piece of your work shows tactical decision impact, and which shows strategic impact? Do not give me the same project twice.
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Show me the project where your research became a specification, not a recommendation.
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Which piece of your work would convince me that research changes decisions rather than documenting them?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: Which project best shows how you shaped an end-to-end experience rather than evaluating a screen?

follow_ups: What in that work was yours specifically, and what was the team's?
What would you cut from that story if you had eight minutes instead of thirty?
Which piece is your weakest, and why do you still lead with it?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior presents strong project work. Lead/Staff curates the work as an argument for a level, separates tactical from strategic influence explicitly, and is precise about personal versus team attribution.

questions.question: We have a few minutes left. What questions do you have for me?
resume_and_role_links: Prepared questions on autonomy uncertainty, shipping velocity, and a strong first six months
JD: shape UX research best practices in Air Defense and across Anduril at large
JD: research operations and repositories
Interview panel: Research, Systems/ML, Product, Design

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: What do you want to ask me about the research function, the bar, or how this team works?
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Anything you want to ask me about the systems, the constraints, or how research and engineering interact here?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: What do you want to know about the roadmap, the pace, or how decisions get made?
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: What would you want to ask me about the design partnership or the operator experience?

follow_ups: That is a question you could ask any company. What do you actually want to know about this one?
What answer to that question would make you less interested in the role?
What is the question you are hesitant to ask?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior asks informed, respectful questions. Lead/Staff asks questions that reveal a point of view — about where research authority sits, what the team refuses to do, and how evidence and velocity are traded — and treats the answer as decision-relevant.

questions.question: The strongest argument against hiring you is that you have never worked in defense. What is your answer?
resume_and_role_links: Career arc across consumer, spaceflight, automotive, and clinical domains
MIL-STD-1472 and NASA-STD-3001 application
Coaching state structural gap: no confirmed direct Air Defense field experience
JD: autonomous counter-drone systems and Lattice OS

persona_adaptations.Dr. Daniella Kim: Name the biggest gap between your background and this role, and tell me how you would close it in the first six months.
persona_adaptations.Systems / ML Engineering Lead: Everything you have worked on had a forgiving failure mode compared with this. Why should I trust your judgment here?
persona_adaptations.Product Manager: Give me the honest case against hiring you, and then tell me why I should anyway.
persona_adaptations.Design Lead: What part of this domain do you genuinely not understand yet?

follow_ups: What is the first thing you would be wrong about here, and how would you find out fast?
Which of your transferable claims does not transfer? Be specific.
If we hire you and it does not work out, what will the reason have been?
questions.lead_staff_bar: Senior deflects the objection with transferable-skills language. Lead/Staff names the real gap precisely, states the boundary of what transfers, and gives a concrete plan with a detection mechanism for being wrong.
